candidates.name: St Jean Cathedral
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 08:15-12:00, 13:45-19:30, Sat Sun 08:15-12:00, 13:45-19:00; services (no visits) Mon-Fri 09:00 and 19:00, Sat 09:00, Sun 08:30 and 10:30 (high mass)
candidates.content: The cathedral is dedicated to St John the Baptist (St Jean-Baptiste) and St Stephen (St Etienne) and has the title of primatiale because the Bishop of Lyon has the honorary title of Primat des Gaules. Built between 1180 and 1480,

candidates.name: St Jean archaeological garden
candidates.content: Next to St Jean cathedral (on the northern side), this small garden shows the remains of the religious buildings which occupied the site before the cathedral was erected. The oldest remains date back to the 4th century (baptistery

candidates.name: Fourvière basilica
candidates.content: Built in 1872 and dedicated to the Virgin Mary, patron saint of Lyon, this massive church made of white marble has been compared to an elephant with its feet up. It is a typical example of the 19th century "eclectic" style, with a

candidates.name: St Irénée church
candidates.hours: Church 08:30-18:00 daily, crypt Sat 14:30-17:00, closed in Aug
candidates.content: The oldest church in Lyon, and one of the oldest in France. The site is built on a Gallo-Roman necropolis which was in use for centuries, until the Middle Ages. Some sarcophagi from the 5th or 6th century are visible in the courty

candidates.name: Church of Saint-Bruno des Chartreux
candidates.content: The only Baroque church in Lyon. The interior is magnificent, especially the altar (by Servandoni, modified by Soufflot, 18th century) and the canopy (by Servandoni).

candidates.name: Basilica of Saint-Martin d'Ainay
candidates.content: The only entirely Romanesque church in Lyon, dating back to the 11th-12th centuries. The abbey of Ainay was one of the most powerful in France between the 13th and the 16th centuries. A must-see for its very nice atmosphere.

candidates.name: Musées Gadagne: Historical museum of Lyon and International puppet museum
candidates.price: 1 museum: €6 including audioguide, 2 museums: €8, 2 museums + temporary exhibition: €10. Under 26 and disabled: free
candidates.content: These museums dedicated to the history of the city and to puppets (like the famous Guignol from Lyon). The building is a magnificent Renaissance palace that is worth a visit. A nice garden and cafe have also been created at the to

candidates.name: Musée Miniature et Cinéma
candidates.content: Created by artist Dan Ohlmann, this private gallery shows about 120 miniature models of all kinds of scenes: houses, restaurants, workshops, schools, etc., from Lyon or elsewhere, historical or contemporary. The accuracy of the mo

candidates.name: Place du Change
candidates.content: The largest square in the area has two remarkable buildings. The Loge du Change, on the west side, was partially built by the great architect Soufflot. It is now a Protestant church known as Temple du Change. It can be visited on

candidates.name: Rue Juiverie
candidates.content: Another typical street of Vieux Lyon. It is named after the Jewish community who settled there but were expelled in the 14th century. Check out the back courtyard at Hôtel Builloud (number 8); it has a magnificent gallery on the f

candidates.name: Metallic tower of Fourvière
candidates.content: Next to the basilica stands a smaller (86 m, 282 ft) replica of the Eiffel Tower, completed in 1894. Its construction was supported by anticlerical people in order to have a non-religious building as the highest point in Lyon, whi

candidates.name: Place des Terreaux
candidates.content: This large square was completely redesigned in the 1990s by the artist Daniel Buren. On the East side stands the City Hall. On the North side, you will find the fountain sculpted by Bartholdi, the 'father' of the Statue of Liberty

candidates.name: Ile Barbe
candidates.content: This charming island on the river Saône is the only inhabited island in Lyon. In the 5th century, one of the first monasteries in Gaul was founded there. It became a powerful Benedictine abbey (from the 9th century) but was finall

candidates.name: Palais Saint-Pierre / Musée des Beaux Arts
candidates.price: €6, reduced €4, under 18, EU students, and some others free, audioguide €3 or free for some
candidates.hours: Mon Wed Thu Sat 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:30-18:00, partial closures 12:00-14:15, ticket office closes 17:30

candidates.name: Musée d'Art contemporain
candidates.price: Full price €9; reduced price €6 for people aged 18 to 25 and for holders of a ticket less than 6 months old purchased at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon; free for under 18s
candidates.content: It holds temporary exhibitions of Contemporary Art, and selections from its permanent collection of more than 1,400 works.

candidates.name: Musée des Confluences
candidates.content: The spectacular building at the confluence of the Rhône and the Saone is built in a deconstructionist style and has expositions on science and mythology.

candidates.name: Jardin des Curiosités
candidates.content: Small garden hidden in the bottom of a street/car park, behind a metallic door. It was designed by Canadian artists in a surrealistic spirit (recalls Magritte or Dali). Also a very nice viewpoint over the southern part of Lyon.

candidates.name: St Paul church
candidates.content: A very nice church, with mixed Romanesque and Gothic styles. The oldest parts are from the 10th century.

candidates.name: Musee d'art religieux
candidates.hours: Daily 10:00-12:30 and 14:00-17:30, closed in January and February
candidates.content: The small museum holds treasures donated to the church for its construction.

candidates.name: Jardin Rosa Mir
candidates.content: This amazing garden was built by a Spanish refugee, Jules Senis, and dedicated to his mother. Senis had cancer and had made the vow of building this garden if he ever came out of the hospital; fortunately, he did. The garden is a

candidates.name: Saint-Nizier Church
candidates.content: Very nice church of flaming Gothic style.

candidates.name: Parc de la Tête d'or
candidates.content: Completed in 1862, this English-style garden is one of the largest and arguably one of the most beautiful urban parks in France. It is a popular place for families as well as joggers. The highlights of the park include the large g

candidates.name: Rue St Jean
candidates.content: This cobblestone pedestrian street is the main axis of the area. It is full of souvenir shops and restaurants mainly intended for tourists. Local people are aware that real good bouchons are extremely rare here. On a sunny Sunday

candidates.name: Rue du Boeuf
candidates.content: Parallel to Rue St Jean, this street is much more quiet and just as beautiful. It also has a number of restaurants, more expensive than in rue St Jean but, on average, much more worth the money.

candidates.name: Montée du Gourguillon
candidates.content: This picturesque montée (sloping street on hillside) starts behind Vieux Lyon metro station and ends quite close to the Roman theatres of Fourvière. It was the main link between the river Saône and the top of Fourvière throughout

candidates.name: Palais de Justice
candidates.content: The historical court house, also named "the 24 columns", was built between 1835 and 1842 by architect Louis-Pierre Baltard. It is a fine example of French "neo-classical" architecture. It now hosts only the criminal court (Cour d'

candidates.name: Roman theatres
candidates.content: These two well-preserved theatres are the most important remnant of the Roman city of Lugdunum. The Gallo-Roman museum was built next to them. The summer festival "Nuits de Fourvière" takes place here every year, which may cause a

candidates.name: Amphithéâtre des Trois Gaules
candidates.content: This Roman theatre is the place where the first Christian martyrs of Gaul were killed. Documents say that it was the largest theatre in Gaul at that time, but nobody knows exactly how far it extends under the neighbouring building

candidates.name: Opera house
candidates.content: The old opera house was completely redesigned by Jean Nouvel in the 1990s and hosts opera and dancing shows, along with a few other concerts (especially jazz) in the smaller "Amphithéâtre" room.

candidates.name: Ninkasi
candidates.content: This is a modern-day institution in Lyon. Ninkasi has two places for live music: Kafé (free shows, essentially electronic music) and Kao (a concert hall dedicated to rock and electronic music). It is also a beer brewery and has ba

candidates.name: Olympique Lyonnais
candidates.content: Successful on the soccer field but massively in debt, so OL were relegated in 2025 to Ligue 2, the second tier. The stadium (capacity 59,000) is in the suburb of Décines 15 km east of city centre. The women's team is also badly in

candidates.name: Auditorium
candidates.content: The Lyon National Orchestra plays in this impressive, modern concert hall which also hosts some jazz and world music concerts.

candidates.name: Transbordeur
candidates.content: The medium-sized hall (capacity 1,500) for rock or popular music concerts.

candidates.name: Maison de la Danse
candidates.content: A theatre dedicated to modern dancing. Also a fine example of architecture of the 1960s.

candidates.name: Théâtre des Célestins
candidates.content: The historical theatre, in a beautiful 19th century building by Gaspard André. Serious programme.

candidates.name: ASVEL
candidates.content: The Villeurbanne basketball team has a long history as one of the major clubs in the country.

candidates.name: Théâtre le Guignol de Lyon
candidates.content: The largest Guignol theatre, showing original creations for children and adults.

candidates.name: Institut Lumière
candidates.content: The museum also has a theatre showing thematic series of cinema masterpieces (in original version). The theatre is in the former Lumière factory, which was the scenery of the first movie in history (La sortie des usines Lumière).

candidates.name: Comoedia
candidates.content: After a few years of closure followed by refurbishment works, this independent cinema is now very comfortable and has a relatively avant-garde programme. All foreign movies are shown in original version.

candidates.name: Pathé
candidates.content: This major national firm has four theatres in Lyon (Cordeliers, Bellecour, Vaise, Carré de Soie) offering essentially American blockbusters and mainstream French movies. The Bellecour branch has foreign films in original version.

candidates.name: UGC
candidates.content: The other major cinema firm, has four theatres in Lyon (Part-Dieu, Cité Internationale, Astoria, Confluence). The Astoria (M: Masséna) has foreign movies in original version.

candidates.name: LOU Rugby
candidates.content: The rugby team of Lyon has bounced between the top two levels of the country's league system (Top 14 and Pro D2) in the 2010s; they have played in Top 14 since 2016–17. The team moved to OL's former home of Stade de Gerland for 20

candidates.name: Théâtre de la Croix-Rousse
candidates.content: 'The other' theatre, with a more avant-garde programme.

candidates.name: TNP
candidates.content: Jean Vilar's spirit of 'popular theatre' lives on in the historically left-wing Villeurbanne.

candidates.name: Théâtre Tête d'Or
candidates.content: This is the only theatre in Lyon showing popular comedies in the Parisian "boulevard" style.

candidates.name: Complexe du Rire
candidates.content: Two rooms and talented young comedians.

candidates.name: Véritable Guignol du Vieux Lyon et du Parc
candidates.hours: Wed Sat Sun, bank and school holidays 15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00
candidates.content: Especially intended for children, this outdoor theatre is in the park, near the lake and the zoo.

candidates.name: La Cave des Voyageurs
candidates.content: Opened over 20 years ago by "Jeannot", the picturesque and loud-mouthed owner of the other bar next door, this small and friendly wine bar has built a wide and interesting selection of several hundred wines over the years. Of cour

candidates.name: Georges Five
candidates.price: Wine by the glass from €3, bottles €18-€3,000
candidates.content: This place was opened by the owner of the wine shop Antic Wine. It has therefore a very wide selection of wines (2,800 references), ranging from small local producers to the most famous and sought-after names. Also top-quality foo

candidates.name: Goudyvins
candidates.content: A few steps away from the busy Place Bellecour, a new friendly place where you can enjoy both local and foreign wines with prices starting at €5-7 for a glass of either "blanc", "rosé", or "rouge". The selection is actually quite

candidates.name: Kelly's Pub
candidates.content: Irish pub, live music on Saturday, Irish music sessions on Thursday, quiz every Monday, pool, darts, Irish and English pub food, air conditioning.

candidates.name: Paddy's Corner
candidates.content: Perfect little pub in the Croix-Rousse area, off the beaten track. Live music sessions every Thursday, Pub Quiz on Tuesdays.

candidates.name: Johnny Walsh's
candidates.content: Nice, authentic Irish pub with good music and some live performances.

candidates.name: Wallace
candidates.content: Comfortable beer and whisky bar with a nice terrace, live sports, pub quiz on Thursdays.

candidates.name: The Smoking Dog
candidates.content: English pub. Pub quiz on Tuesdays. Air conditioning.

candidates.name: Hot Club de Lyon
candidates.content: Jazz club (since 1948), in an old typical cellar, with good live jazz 5 nights/week.

candidates.name: Le Fruit Defendu
candidates.content: A great little hole-in-the-wall bar, good for beers and cocktails, and a great place to start the night! Try the Stella with a shot of orange liquor!

candidates.name: Sirius
candidates.content: Live events almost every day of the week. On weekends, there are two dancefloors with all kinds of music. No dress code! Nice.

candidates.name: Vercoquin
candidates.content: See "Buy".

candidates.name: L'Abreuvoir
candidates.content: There you can join some crazy French listening to crazy French music. Definitely an experience, though not everyone's cup of tea.

candidates.name: Le Perroquet Bourré
candidates.content: Cheap rum, the inside is decorated as a pirate ship.

candidates.name: Paul Bocuse
candidates.content: The home base of the master of all chefs, "Monsieur Paul", this restaurant held 3 Michelin stars for a record 55 years, dropping to two only after his death in 2018. Classic French cuisine, with an extortionate price tag; by all a

candidates.name: Le Potager des Halles
candidates.price: If you want cheaper but just as good, try Le Bistrot du Potager next door, where the same owners serve Spanish-style tapas which are a great value for money (no reservations)
candidates.content: This restaurant serves traditional French cuisine made from very good and very fresh products, with a Mediterranean influence. The chocolate fondant dessert is amazing. Very good wine list too. The lunch menu is an absolute steal.

candidates.name: Brasserie Georges
candidates.content: An exceptional traditional brasserie, serving both traditional Lyonnaise food as well as Alsatian favorites like the Choucroute Impériale, a huge pile of sauerkraut with various sausages and an entire pork knuckle. The cavernous m

candidates.name: Pitaya Thaï Street Food
candidates.content: A dive into the streets of Bangkok and its colourful and tasty street food. Fresh and quality products cooked in the wok at the moment in front of your eyes. Delicious and generous dishes.

candidates.name: Le Layon
candidates.hours: Daily lunch and dinner. Serves all day (12:00-00:00) on Sat and Sun
candidates.content: In another street full of tourist traps, this restaurant offers very good, classical local and French cuisine. Try the grenouilles (frogs). Very nice terrace. Good wine list at interesting prices.

candidates.name: Balthaz'Art
candidates.content: Croix-Rousse has more and more interesting restaurants, and this one is a fine example. In a "flea-market-meets-art-gallery" decor, you will enjoy a fresh and creative cuisine with Mediterranean and Asian influences. Nice wine lis

candidates.name: L'Art et la Manière
candidates.content: Small no-tourist restaurant in a no-tourist area. Friendly yet professional service, short menu but very creative, high-quality cooking. Good (although short) wine list. The best bottles are at amazingly low prices given their "co

candidates.name: Prairial
candidates.content: Modern, inventive Michelin-starred haute cuisine, served only as a degustation set menu: the 5-course "Confluence" (€99, lunch only) or the full 8-course "Prairial" (€135). Expect local, seasonal produce, heavy on vegetables and s

candidates.name: Chez Mounier
candidates.content: A traditional bouchon (restaurant) with good food.

candidates.name: Boulangerie du Palais
candidates.content: In this small bakery, you will find good praline tarts, a popular local dessert.

candidates.name: Chez M'man
candidates.content: French cuisine, typical Lyonnais dishes and excellent hospitality. It's a well-run establishment near Place Bellecour. A picturesque place in an endearing environment.

candidates.name: Boulangerie Chez Jules St Paul
candidates.content: Small boulangerie near the historic centre with a great variety of breads, cakes, sandwiches, pizza, salads. There is also the possibility to sit down. Very good croissant aux almond. Also nice to have breakfast. Warm welcome.

candidates.name: Croix-Rousse market
candidates.content: Very popular and typical market mith many local producers. On Tuesdays, also sells non-food items. Very crowded on sunny Sundays, but this is the right time to enjoy the particular mood of the neighbourhood.

candidates.name: St Antoine Market
candidates.content: The other major market, in a wealthier part of town. Also some local fruit and vegetable producers. Eating oysters by the Saône is a very pleasant occupation before Sunday lunch.

december.text: The Festival of Lights (Fête des Lumières) is by far the most important event of the year. It lasts four days around the 8th of December. It was initially a traditional religious celebration: on December 8, 1852, the people of Lyon spontaneously illuminated their windows with candles to celebrate the inauguration of th

The Biennals: Lyon alternatively hosts a dancing (even years) and a contemporary art (odd years) biennals from September to December/January. The dancing biennal is traditionally opened by a street parade in which inhabitants of the Greater Lyon take part through neighbourhood associations. If you are in town at this m

The 200-year-old Guignol is a very famous character of puppet theatre. This irreverent canut who frequently challenges the law in his adventures was created by Laurent Mourguet, a canut himself, in 1808. The main side characters in Guignol shows are his wife Madelon, his Beaujolais-drinking friend Gnafron and the polic

The usual hours for downtown shopping are 10:00-19:00, Monday to Saturday. Some larger places close a bit later (19:30). Shops are closed on Sundays, except in December and in Vieux Lyon where Sunday is the busiest day of the week!

Parc des Hauteurs: This park between the metal tower of Fourvière and the Loyasse cemetery is a promenade with a nice footbridge offering great views towards the Monts d'Or and Beaujolais. There is an aerial adventure course and a skiing and mountain bike slope.
